{{Short description|Edges crossing all dicuts in a directed graph}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=November 2022}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=November 2022}}

[[File:Dijoin.svg|thumb|upright=0.8|When either of the red or blue sets of edges are [[edge contraction|contracted]], the resulting graph becomes [[strongly connected graph|strongly connected]]. This means that each of these is a dijoin.]]

In mathematics, a '''dijoin''' is a subset of the edges of a [[directed graph]], with the property that [[edge contraction|contracting]] every edge in the dijoin produces a [[strongly connected graph]]. Equivalently, a dijoin is a subset of the edges that, for every [[dicut]], includes at least one edge contained in the dicut. Here, a dicut is a set of edges in a directed graph, defined from a partition of the vertices into two subsets, so that each edge that has an endpoint in both subsets is directed from the first subset to the second.

[[Woodall's conjecture]], an unsolved problem in this area, states that in any directed graph the minimum number of edges in a dicut (the unweighted minimum closure) equals the maximum number of disjoint dijoins that can be found in the graph (a packing of dijoins).{{r|acz|woodall}} A fractional weighted version of the conjecture, posed by [[Jack Edmonds]] and Rick Giles, was refuted by [[Alexander Schrijver]].{{r|eg|schrijver|acz}}

The [[Lucchesi–Younger theorem]] states that the minimum size of a dijoin, in any given directed graph, equals the maximum number of disjoint dicuts that can be found in the graph.{{r|lovasz|ly}} The minimum weight dijoin in a weighted graph can be found in [[polynomial time]],{{r|frank}} and is a special case of the [[submodular flow]] problem.{{r|gabow}}

In [[planar graph]]s, dijoins and [[feedback arc set]]s are dual concepts. The [[dual graph]] of a directed graph, embedded in the plane, is a graph with a vertex for each face of the given graph, and a dual edge between two dual vertices when the corresponding two faces are separated by an edge. Each dual edge crosses one of the original graph edges, turned by 90° clockwise.  A feedback arc set is a subset of the edges that includes at least one edge from every directed cycle. For a dijoin in the given graph, the corresponding set of edges forms a directed cut in the dual graph, and vice versa.{{r|gab95}} This relationship between these two problems allows the feedback arc set problem to be solved efficiently for planar graphs, even though it is [[NP-hard]] for other types of graphs.{{r|frank}}
